title: SQL Injection via String Template in rawQuery
platform_conditions: Android runtime (API level 1+ for SQLiteDatabase.rawQuery and execSQL)
security_mechanism: SQLiteDatabase.rawQuery and execSQL execute the statement text as given; a Kotlin string template ('... WHERE id = \'$id\'') splices the value into the SQL before the database parser sees it, so a value containing a quote or SQL syntax changes the statement structure. Local SQLite injection is not limited to one app's rows: providers and databases often hold cross-user or synced data, and injection in a query feeding CursorAdapter/content-provider results leaks rows the caller should not read. The '?' placeholder + selectionArgs form binds the value out-of-band and cannot alter the parse.

source_sink_clues.source: Deep-link parameters, Intent extras, content-provider URIs, or IPC values from other apps that reach the query through uri.lastPathSegment or query parameters.
source_sink_clues.sink: db.rawQuery / db.execSQL / SQLiteQueryBuilder query built with Kotlin string templates or concatenation instead of selectionArgs

tracking_guards: Check the statement uses the placeholder form (rawQuery(sql with '?', arrayOf(value)) or SQLiteQueryBuilder with selectionArgs); identifiers that cannot be bound (column names, ORDER BY) must come from a fixed allowlist; for ContentProvider openFile/query, check uri.lastPathSegment is validated against an allowlist or pattern before being spliced into a path or query.
not_candidate_when: The value travels in selectionArgs (placeholder binding), the interpolated part is a server/app-internal constant chosen from an allowlist, or the input is strictly validated to a narrow grammar (integer ID) before reaching the query.
synthetic_vulnerable_example: db.rawQuery("SELECT * FROM items WHERE id = '$id'", null)
synthetic_safe_example: db.rawQuery("SELECT * FROM items WHERE id = ?", arrayOf(id))
public_references: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in SQL Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html
